content.subject: Implement dynamic map modification API in simulator
content.description: Add modify_obstacles (and status/change-history query) to FleetSimulator with strict validation: int pairs, bounds, no add+remove conflict, no covering robots; batch dedup; no-op no record; no tick/position/distance change; reroute assigned tasks; pause on unreachable.

content.subject: Implement rerouting, pause/resume and step-time recovery
content.description: After map change: assigned unfinished tasks keep robots; unpicked replan current->pickup->dropoff with pickup confirmed first if already there; picked only route to dropoff; unreachable clears route and pauses; unpause at step start when reachability returns; blocked routes also handled defensively in step.

content.subject: Add replay map-change frames and public queries
content.description: Replay retains position/completion frames; add map-change event records at effective tick with adds/removes cells preserving intra-tick batch order; frames immutable to later maps. Public query surfaces current obstacles and paused task ids distinct from waiting-for-right-of-way.

content.subject: Checkpoint v2 with map, pause state, change history; v1 compat
content.description: Bump checkpoint version to 2; persist current map, paused state, map_changes history; v1 files still load with no map-change history; validate change coords/bounds/add-remove conflicts and replayed map matches saved map; keep atomic save and CLI error behavior.

content.subject: Add tests and update README docs
content.description: Cover validation errors/atomicity, rerouting/pause/resume, replay order and immutability, checkpoint v2 round trip + v1 compat + corrupt-history ValueError, determinism, CLI demo/resume still work. Update README format docs.

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Dynamic map edits
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def modify_obstacles(
        self,
        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.

        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
        and leave every part of the state untouched.

        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
        distance is accumulated.
        """
        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
        if conflict:
            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
            raise ValueError(
                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
            )
        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
        for cell in add_cells:
            if cell in occupied:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
                )
        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)

    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
        seen: set[Position] = set()
        ordered: list[Position] = []
        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
            if not self.grid.contains(position):
                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
            if position in seen:
                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
                continue
            seen.add(position)

Implementation complete. All 75 tests pass (32 pre-existing, now updated to v2; plus a new 43-case module). Here's what was delivered.

## What changed

**`warehouse_fleet/simulator.py`** — the core feature:

- **`modify_obstacles(added=..., removed=...)`** — public batch edit between ticks. Whole-batch validation up front (must be `[int, int]` pairs, booleans rejected, in-bounds, no add/remove overlap, no obstacle on a robot's current cell); any failure raises `ValueError` with map/routes/tasks/stats/history untouched. In-batch duplicates collapse to one; adding an existing obstacle / removing a free cell is a no-op; a no-effect batch writes no record. Accepted edits change the map immediately but never advance the tick, move a robot, or add distance.
- **Rerouting & pause** — assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot. Uncollected robots replan current→pickup→dropoff; carrying robots route only to dropoff (a reclosed pickup never pulls them back). Any unreachable leg/endpoint clears the route and suspends the task in `paused_tasks`; the robot can't drive the stale route, and the task is neither released nor completed. Unassigned unreachable tasks just keep waiting. The next `step()` after reopening auto-resumes driving and assignment; collision avoidance still forbids entering new obstacles (plus a defensive re-plan guard).
- **Queries/replay** — `status()` shows current obstacles and map-paused task ids (distinct from traffic right-of-way waiting); `map_change_history()` gives each actual edit. Replay keeps original tick frames untouched and interleaves `map_change` events carrying effective tick, global sequence (preserving same-tick order), and added/removed cells. Deterministic throughout.
- **Checkpoints** — bumped to **version 2**, adding `base_grid`, `map_changes`, and `paused_tasks`; strict validation of change coordinates, add/remove conflicts, sequence/tick ordering, replay↔history agreement, history-reproduces-saved-grid, and a genuinely-unreachable paused state. **Version 1 files still load** (verified against a file written by the original code) with empty edit history; saves stay atomic and CLI error behavior is unchanged.

**`README.md`** — documented the edit API, semantics, queries, and the v2 format with v1 compatibility. **`tests/test_simulator.py`** — version assertions updated; **`tests/test_dynamic_map.py`** — new module covering validation/all-or-nothing semantics, rerouting/pause/resume, no-return-to-closed-pickup, waiting tasks, right-of-way distinction, replay ordering/immutability, determinism, interrupted-run parity at edit boundaries, instance independence, and checkpoint v2/v1/corruption cases. `demo`/`resume` and all existing Python entry points still work, including exact demo↔resume snapshot parity.
